thread:
mara_ops: Heads up — iterating on a mixed-capacity design for eu-west1 inference pools. Proposal: min on-demand floor ~60% of steady-state for critical routes, allow spot burst for the remainder. Want thoughts on routing/fallback and interruption handling. TL;DR: keep latency-critical traffic on demand, burst stateless jobs to spot. cc @samir_infra @li-chen

samir_infra: +1 on the split. A couple practical notes: 1) compute floor from a 7d rolling p50 of sustained QPS (not peak). 2) express floor both as percentage and absolute min instances so tiny services don’t go to zero. e.g. min_on_demand = max(ceil(steady*0.6), 3)

li-chen: important callout: cross-region fallback can blow up egress and add 30–60ms. prefer region-local burst first, then failover to nearby region only for stateless low-SLA requests. For stateful flows we must keep >80% on-demand local or degrade gracefully.

anna_product: For enterprise customers with 99p latency SLA we should tag routes and reserve dedicated on-demand capacity. We can also surface a per-route "latency_class" so the router pins to on-demand pools by tag.

samir_infra: interruption handling: plan is to drain + fence off new requests, then checkpoint KV cache and active sessions. Steps: 1) mark instance DRAINING, 2) move streaming requests to fallback on-demand or replicate session to sibling instance, 3) persist minimal state to redis, 4) let preemptible be reclaimed. We must keep drain timeout small (20–45s) to not hold up autoscaler.

mara_ops: here's a rough policy sketch we tested in dev. thoughts?

```yaml
policy_name: mixed-eu-infer
steady_state_window_days: 7
min_on_demand_ratio: 0.6
min_on_demand_instances: 3
burst_pool:
  max_spot_ratio: 0.5
  preemptible_grace_sec: 30
  allow_cross_region_burst: false
fallback:
  route: nearest-compatible-model
  max_cross_region_latency_ms: 60
```

li-chen: config looks reasonable. Suggest adding `region_capacity_safety` to avoid exhausting GPU quotas during rapid scaleups (we hit quota in ap-southeast once). Also add `billing_tag_on_interrupt: true` so we track interruption cost per job.

samir_infra: agree on quota guard. Operationally we should have a small hot spare pool (1–2 on-demand nodes) per AZ to absorb spot churn while autoscaler provisions new on-demand. That spare should be outside normal scaling policies so it's not stolen.

anna_product: UI/observability: expose token-level routing decisions in Console (why request went to spot vs on-demand) + an interruption reason field so SREs can correlate regressions to spot churn.

mara_ops: one more ops nit: implement a cheap health check for model warmup — if spot instance comes up but model load > X ms, route first N requests to fallback until warm. Avoid cold-start tail spikes.

infra-bot: Deploy triggered: mixed-pool-policy v0.3 -> staging (sha: a1b2c3). Runbook: /runbooks/mixed-pools.md

samir_infra: action items: 1) samir -> add quota safety & hot-spare logic to autoscaler PR (ETA EOD Tue). 2) li-chen -> add billing tag on interrupt + region constraints to policy (ETA Wed). 3) mara_ops -> draft fallback runbook and drain scripts (ETA Thu).

mara_ops: cool — if we land this, expect ~25–40% cost savings for stateless workloads in eu-west1 while keeping critical SLAs intact. Will share benchmarks after staging run. :rocket:
